summary.text: Valerie Foushee is the Democratic U.S. representative for North Carolina's 4th Congressional District, and is seeking re-election. A Chapel Hill native, she worked for the Chapel Hill Police Department for 21 years and held local office on the school board and Orange County Board of Commissioners before serving in the state legislature. She was elected to Congress in 2022 and serves on the Science, Space, and Technology and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

paragraphs.text: Valerie Foushee was born in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, in 1956.
According to her official biography, she grew up in Chapel Hill as the oldest of six children of parents who had left high school to raise the family.

She attended the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill for two years before withdrawing for financial reasons, then returned and graduated in 2008 with a bachelor's degree in political science and Afro and African-American studies.
She joined the Chapel Hill Police Department as an administrative officer in 1987 and retired in 2008 after 21 years. She also held administrative positions with insurance and research companies.
Foushee served on the Chapel Hill-Carrboro City school board from 1997 to 2004, chairing it from 2001 to 2003.
She then served on the Orange County Board of Commissioners from 2004 to 2012 (chair 2008-2010), and her official biography says she was the first African American woman to chair the commission.
She served in the North Carolina General Assembly, in the House for District 50 in 2013 and then in the State Senate for District 23 from 2013 to 2023, succeeding Eleanor Kinnaird.

Foushee won the Democratic primary for the open 4th District seat in May 2022 and the November 2022 general election, and her official biography says she is the first African American and first woman to represent the district.
She was renominated in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Nida Allam and Mary Patterson.

In Congress she serves on the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee (Ranking Member of the Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee; Energy Subcommittee) and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (Aviation and Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials subcommittees).
